findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

An employee was observed to change gloves without washing their hands and immediately moving to preparing a sandwich. Raw chicken was handled prior to this glove change. Education was conducted and the hands washed to correct. Ensure that hand washing takes place at all times required by the code.

4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the dish machine would not produce a color change on the inspector’s test strips. Investigation revealed an empty container of sanitizer concentrate. The PIC was shown and had the jug replaced. A recheck later in the inspection still showed no color change on the chemical test strips. Education was conducted in relation to priming the machine. The machine was primed by the inspector and registered correctly afterwards.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY (TCS) FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above.

Cheese sauce is observed in the far right well of the steam table and with an internal temperature of 128F. The cook was consulted and stated that the items came from the cooking process recently. This was supported by other observations made during the inspection. This container is the only item in this well and the other side is open. It is believed that this is the issue and that was stated to the cook. A lid was added to the back side to trap in the escaping heat. The cheese was allowed to be brought back up to temperature to save it and correct the violation. Ensure that all hot held TCS foods are maintained at 135F or hotter at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding.
findings.citation_text:
3-403.11(A) Reheating for Hot Holding. (A) Except as specified under (B) and (C) and in (E) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding shall be reheated so that all parts of the FOOD reach a temperature of at least 74°C (165°F) for 15 seconds. 

A pan of cheese sauce on the prep line was observed at 114F internal temperature during this inspection. Investigation showed that it was pulled from its reheating process to early due to a miscommunication in the kitchen. The cheese was on the cook line approximately 30-45 minutes prior to observation per the cook that pulled it. The pan was allowed to be brought to the stove for rapid reheating to be saved. Another pan was above 165F and moved to the steam table for service to correct. Ensure that the reheating process is completed each time in the facility.

1) During the inspection, there was a significant amount of food noted in the walk-in cooler lacking date marking and out of temperature. The food was then moved in to the walk-in cooler, thusly why it was found out of temperature in the walk-in. 2) A multitude of items were noted, in the walk-in cooler and the prep cooler, to be without date marking. Ensure that PHFs are date marked and used within 7 days. Items stored in the prep cooler can have a bulk reference point in the walk-in cooler, such as lunch meats. This bulk items were not in the walk-in cooler though. Once the product is depleted, then make sure the date mark is transferred to the product inside the prep cooler. 3) Observed pepperoni being stored in the walk-in cooler with date of 2/24 and 3/5. This is past the 7 days and should be discarded. Ensure that RTE PHFs are used or discarded within 7 days. Items were date marked, pepperoni discarded, and the PHFs from the prep cooler were discarded during the inspection. 
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

Observed multiple personal drinks and items being stored on the cutting board at the prep cooler. Ensure that there are sufficient spaces provided for employee personal drinks and items. Personal drinks should be stored below and away from food and food surfaces. They should also be provided with a lid and a straw. The cutting board was taken to dish to be washed, rinsed, then santized, and returned to service. 
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the meat slicer blade to have an excessive accumulation of food debris. 2) Ice machine baffles noted to have a mold accumulation. 3) Observed the clean dish rack by the dish washing machine to have food debris on it. Ensure that food contact surfaces are washed, rinsed, and santized after each use. 
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the hot holding cabinet to have an accumulation of food debris inside of it and it was not in service during the inspection. Ensure that the non-food surfaces are regularly washed, rinsed, and sanitized to prevent accumulations of debris. 
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed the hand sink in the prep area to not have paper towels upon entering the facility. Ensure that a supply of sanitary towels are provided at each hand washing sink. Paper towels provided during the inspection. 
750-1120e A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed a considerable hole in the wall in a room thats in the rear of the facility. This room is utilized to store paper towels and chemicals. Ensure that walls and ceilings are maintained smooth, as well as easily cleanable. 
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Approved source
findings.comment:

Drain and replace the fryer oil and clean the fryers.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Clean al non-food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: Clean the walls.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed house made ranch in the soft drink cooler, near the service line, to be probed at 55F. This cooler is not holding at adequate temperatures (air temp of 48F) and should have all PHFs removed until the cooler is fixed has been inspected by an HVAC professional. The ranch was prepared yesterday. It is unsure when the ranch came out of temperature, so the ranch was discarded, voluntarily, during the inspection. 
750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed ground meats being stored over whole, intact steaks in the walk-in cooler. Ensure that the ground meats are placed below the steaks in order to prevent cross-contamination. Meats were moved into proper order during the inspection. 
750-130(d)  All raw meat shall be properly stored, store in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature product on the bottom.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Observed an employee wash their hands, then turn off the faucet without using a barrier. Employee was stopped, educated, and instructed to rewash hands. Ensure that a barrier is utilized to turn off the faucet to prevent recontamination of hands. 
750-510d To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Observed the dish machine to not test for any sanitizer. Dish machine was primed for 2 minutes without change in sanitizer levels. Manager contacted MJ Kellner, who responded to the facility. MJ Kellner staff replaced the tubing throughout the sanitizer setup, which caused the sanitizer to begin flowing freely again. Dish machine tested at 100 ppm of Chlorine. Ensure that the dish machine is checked at regular intervals for sanitizer concentrations. This will help to ensure that the machine is operating properly. 
750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed areas in the kitchen to be without coving. Ensure that coving is provided and repaired to not allow for openings between the flooring and the wall. 
750-1200 The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
1) Observed meat sauce in the walk-in cooler that was dated 7/3/2017. This is outside of the 7 day window and should have been discarded on 07/10/2017 at the end of service. 2) Observed pepperoni and sausage in the prep cooler next to the oven that were probed at 55-58F (probed). Ensure that RTE PHFs are maintained at 41F or below and discarded within 7 days of the start of service. Items discarded during the inspection. 
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed cooked chicken in the hot wells at 125-130F (probed) at approximately 11:35 AM. The chicken was cooked and placed into the hot holding at 11:00 AM. Ensure that the hot holding wells are maintaining proper temperatures to hold food at 135F or above. All other foods in the steam wells, besides violation 3c, were right at 135-140F. Ensure that the hot holding wells are working appropriately. The chicken had 4 hour time marks placed on it and will be used or discarded by 3:00 PM. 
750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.)

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.comment:
Observed meat sauce in the hot well that was at 130F when probed. After speaking with manager, he stated he believed it was not reheated properly since the meat sauce had just been placed into service. Ensure that PHFs are reheated to 165F within 2 hours of starting the reheating process. Manager instructed the cooks to place the meat sauce back on the stove to reheat to a higher temperature.
750-210  Potentially hazardous foods shall be reheated rapidly to 165°F or higher through out the product. Properly reheat food to 165°F or above.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
Observed 2.5 gallons of shell pasta, 5 gallons of yellow cheese, and 10 gallons of white cheese that were made yesterday. The probed temperatures of the cheeses discarded ranged from 46-50F. The probed temperature of the shell pasta was 83F. Products listed were discarded. Ensure that shallow pans are used during the cooling process, as well as utilizing the ice paddles in the facility. Proper SOPs should be established to ensure the facility is cooling properly at all times. 
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed single service on the cook line to be stored with the food contact surface side up. Ensure that the single service is stored in a manner that prevents potentials for cross contamination. The single service items were inverted during the inspection. 
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
1) Observed the walk-in cooler to have multiple items that were out of temperature. The cooler's air temperature was reading at 50-53F (multiple thermometers referenced). There was a log sheet from this morning that stated the temperature of the walk-in was at 38F. The manager was instructed to have an employee go through and temperature check all items that were refrigerated PHFs that had not come in on this morning's truck. Ground beef, chili, cut tomatoes, meat sauce, prime rib, taco meat, and cabbage were among the items discarded by the employee. The internal temperatures of those items ranged from 45F-50F. 2) There was pizza sauce in the walk-in cooler that had a date of 3/12 with a laddle in it as if it was still being served. The pizza sauce is made in house. Any refrigerated PHFs should be discarded 7 days after the date it was opened or made. 
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Walk-in cooler had an air temperature of 50-53F (multiple thermometers referenced). The employees stated that a box must have hit the thermostat and pushed it up because it was set at 45F. Employee turned the thermostat back down and the walk-in freezer door was opened to assist in cooling the walk-in. 
750-140 All refrigeration units used to store potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41°F or below.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
1) Observed the walk-in cooler to be in general disorganization. There was raw meat over cooked meat. Eggs were over produce and other ready to eat items. This is improper storage organization. The manager was instructed to reorganize the items into their proper storage orders, which the manager noted that she was aware of. 2) Observed a paddle, used for kettles, sitting in a rack and an employee acknowledged it had not been used today. The paddle had food debris noted on it. This presents a potential for cross contamination since the paddle was not properly cleaned and then placed back into service. Ensure that when washing dishes that all food debris is removed. 3) The handle of an ice scoop was noted sitting in the ice. This presents a potential for cross contamination as employees touch many items, then grab the ice scoop and place it back in the ice. Ensure that if the ice scoop is being stored that it is with the handle extended, or on a clean dry surface. Ice scoop was removed, washed, rinsed, and sanitized, then set back into service in the proper manner. 
750-130(d)  All raw meat shall be properly stored, store in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature product on the bottom.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed multiple containers of food within the walk-in cooler, that had finished the cooling process, without a lid or protective cover. Ensure that protective covers are provided, after finishing the cooling process, to prevent cross contamination from other items. 
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Observed an employee, on the cook line, task switching and touching many different non-food contact surfaces, then grabbed ready to eat toast and placed it on a plate with the same gloves. Employee was instructed that this was improper and that the toast should be discarded, gloves removed, and his hands washed prior to donning a new pair of gloves. Ensure that when task switching that gloves are changed when they may have been potentially contaminated. 
750-160bGloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interuption in operations.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
1) Observed an employee shake, in a Steak N' Shake cup, in the walk-in freezer, above ready to eat ice cream. The lid had a fairly large gap noted, shake lid. 2) Observed an employee drink sitting on top of a prep cooler by the grill. Ensure that personal drinks are placed in a designated area that is below and away from food with a lid and a straw. Both drinks were discarded during the inspection. 
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the ice machines in the rear of the facility to have duct tape and foil as a repair surface. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces, if repaired, are repaired in a manner that keeps a smooth, easily cleanable surface. These surfaces should be removed  and properly repaired as to allow for proper cleaning. 
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed the wrapping of utensils in a manner that allowed for the food contact surfaces to be exposed. Ensure that when wrapping utensils they are wrapped in a way that does not leave the food contact surface side exposed. 
750-870 Tableware may be set prior to serving a meal when glasses and cups are inverted, and knives, forks and spoons are wrapped or otherwise covered.
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed single-service items on the cook line that were stored with the food contact surface up with no cover. Ensure that single-service articles are stored in a manner that prevents contamination of the food contact surface. Proper storage is under cover or inverted. The items were inverted during the inspection. 
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained

750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed raw salmon sitting above cabbage in the upright cooler. Ensure that foods are stored in the proper order as to prevent contamination of ready to eat foods from raw foods. 
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed pizza dough in the freezer to be sitting on the shelf touching the bare metal. No bag or box appeared to be near the area for protection. Ensure food is protected at all times.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

Make sure that dish operator is washing hands between handling dirty dishes and other tasks and going to handle clean dishes.

Store glasses in such a manner as to eliminate the potential for cross-contamination should spillage occur.  Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - A) Several cooked potentially hazardous foods were in the process of cooling in the walkin freezer. Today's date was documented on the foods, but time of cooling was not present. Two different containers of noodles were observed with surface temperatures of 48F-50F (lid on/askew on container) and 8F-36F (no lid on container) and internal temperatures of for noodles were at 82F and 102F. Cooked chicken wings in a stainless steel pan had surface and internal temperatures of 83F-90F and 98F respectively, and marinara in a 5 gallon bucket had surface and internal temperatures of 90F and 162F respectively. Cook was advised on better practices for rapid cooling, as well as proper labeling of date and time for cooling foods. Cook noted all foods were prepared within the last hour and just placed in the walkin freezer. Cook began portioning, stirring and checking temperatures to help ensure proper cooling.
Cooked foods must be monitored during the cooling process to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frame for proper cooling (135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and 70F to 41F/below in an additional 4hrs; total time must not exceed 6 hrs). Utilize ice wands and ice baths, place foods in small portions and then combine after foods reach 41F/below, and check temperatures with clean, calibrated stem thermometers during the cooling process.
Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F.

B) Dressing portions just prepared were not labeled as to date of prep. Date was added to the storage container.
Label foods with date of prep.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - A) Ranch dressing and sour cream portions in the upright dressing cooler were observed at temperatures of 43F, 45F, and 50F, with the products in the bottom of the cooler having the highest temperatures. All portions in the bottom of the cooler observed above 45F were discarded in the trash. Other portions at 43F and 45F were kept in the top half of the cooler for use. The bottom half of the cooler was not maintaining temperature (potential issue with air circulation - see #4 below). 

B) Foods in the walkin cooler were observed with surface temperatures at 46F-50F and internal temperatures of 45F-56F. Voluntary order of destruction was completed and all foods with temperatures above 45F were discarded (see order of destruction for details). Refrigeration technician arrived during inspection (see #4 below). Foods that did not have to be discarded were able to be kept in the walkin due to repairs being completed during inspection. 

Cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) must be maintained at proper product temperature at all times during storage (41F/below).

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Walkin cooler was observed at 48F-51F and was unable to maintain several PHF at proper temperature (see #3a, part B above). Call for service was made (see general comments). Refrigeration technician arrived during inspection and was able to make repairs. The thermostat needed to be adjusted, and the walkin dropped to 34F during inspection.

NOTE: The upright dressing cooler was also checked and needed to have Freon added. The technician had to go buy a part in order to finish repairs to the upright dressing cooler.

All refrigeration units used to store PHF shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41F/below.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated

750.160 - Condensation was observed puddling in the bottom of the reach-in dressing cooler. Some condensate was observed puddling in containers holding dressing portions. Portion cups sitting in condensate were discarded. A part has been ordered to repair the upright dressing cooler. 

Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Garnish tray in bar cooler and pizza crusts in walkin freezer were uncovered. 

Foods shall be properly stored and protected at all times. Cover foods between uses and during long term/overnight storage.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)

An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection. Personal drinks must be in a cup with a lid and a straw and also stored/handled in a manner that will not pose a risk of cross contamination.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Quat test strips were observed to be water damaged. Test strips were discarded. Obtain a new set of quat test strips for checking wall mounted chemical dispenser.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - Wall mounted sanitizer dispenser was not working properly. Freshly made sani-buckets had a concentration of 0ppm quat. One employee stated the product did not seem to be pulling through the line. The tubing was loose, and inspector asked the owner to see if he could get the suction functioning again. Owner noted he would call a technician for service. In the meantime, staff used bleach to make buckets (200ppm).

Maintain bleach solutions in buckets at 100-200ppm chlorine. Once wall mounted dispenser is repaired the staff may once again fill sani-buckets from the dispenser. Use test strips to verify quat sanitizer is maintained at 200ppm.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) BAR - soda gun nozzle and holder  (mold);
B) baffles inside ice machines (mold);   and
C) can opener blade (food debris).

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs of continuous use, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

A) BAR - 1. inside cabinet beneath Killian's draft beer (sticky splash/buildup), 2. gray tub holding wrapped silverware and single service crackers (crumbs/debris), 3. inside 2 door reach-in cooler (mold/splash/debris - bottom, shelving, and back wall), 4. bottom inside beer cooler with Corona light (liquid/debris), and 5. speed rails (splash/debris);   and

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - A) The floor at the bar was soiled with debris and/or mold under the ice bin, around the motor beneath the soda gun, along the walls behind/under equipment, and around the cleanup cap next to the floor drain under the 3 part sink.

B) Floor drain beneath the dish machine and the plumbing above it were soiled with splash and buildup.

C) Floor and coving behind the soda syrup boxes were soiled with buildup and debris.

Clean the floors in the aforementioned areas and maintain them clean.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean

B) Hood/baffles over fryers and cook line were soiled with buildup. Get the hood/baffles cleaned.

Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750.160  Observed a dry cloth being used to wipe down a thermometer after the stem  was used to check the internal temperature of a lasagna. While the monitoring of temperatures is an awesome practice and is appreciated, make sure that the stem thermometer is being properly sanitized between uses. The stem thermometer was wiped with a sanitized cloth during the inspection. Make sure the stem portion is also washed, rinsed, and sanitized at least every four hours (or as frequently as necessary to maintain clean and free of gross food debris).
findings.citation_text:
750.120  Slicer in back prep area was observed to be soiled and had a portion of cheese left on it. Cook stated he sliced cheese this morning. Some of the food debris on the back side of the blade was dried, pieces of what appeared to be onion, which was not sliced this morning. Cook was advised on cleaning and sanitizing of the slicer. Detachable pieces were taken to dish area to go through ware washing. The remainder of the slicer must be manually washed, rinsed, and sanitized.
Clean and sanitize the slicer between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use, to prevent potential cross contamination and eliminate buildup of food debris.

Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
750-120(a)) Observed a block of cheese in the base of the first preparation cooler (across from cooler) to not be properly covered. Food was in contact with the cooler's metal shelving. 750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.
Store Single-service items properly.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed that the waste containers in the rest rooms did not have covers on them.
750-1110d Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors. A supply of toilet tissue shall be provided at each toilet at all times. Easily clean able, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.
Provide covers for waste receptacles.

findings.title: Water source safe, hot, and cooled under pressure
findings.comment:
Observed that the hand washing sink by the dish machine has hot water but the valve is stuck/inoperable so that it does not provide cold water.
1120-Each lavatory shall be provided with hot and cold running water.
Repair faucet.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Flies were still present in the establishment.
1160- Effective measures to control insects shall be implemented.
Provide means of effective pest control.

findings.title: Rooms and equipment - vented as required
findings.comment:
The vent hood is still not operating correctly.
1250-All rooms shall have sufficient ventilation.
Provide adequate ventilation.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.comment:
The prep cooler by the cookline was blowing air at 50 degrees.  Repair the prep cooler so it holds below 41 degrees by the assigned date.
750-140 All refrigeration units used to store potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41°F or below.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Numerous flies were observed through out the kitchen area.  Contact Adams pest control (current pest control provider) to get rid of the flies by the assigned date.
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Rooms and equipment - vented as required
findings.comment:
The hood vent system was not removing the hot air in the kitchen.  A new motor has been ordered and should be installed by the assigned date.
750-1250 All rooms shall have sufficient ventilation to keep them free of excessive, heat, steam, condensation, vapors, obnoxious odors, smoke, and fumes. Provide adequate ventilation.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed pans of meat and soup in the walk-in cooler that were not labeled. 750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F. Properly label all PHF.
Observed a pan of flour that was not labeled with the commo0n name of product. 750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name. Properly label all bulk food containers.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment:
Observed that the prep table across from grill and the freezer near prep area did not contain thermometers.  R750.150(a) All hot units that contain potentially hazardous foods shall contain  a conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F
Provide thermometers in  refrigeration units.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment: Observed that the drain from the new dishwashing machine is causing flooding around the floor drain. 750-1100(b) Drain lines from equipment shall not discharge waste water in such a manner as will permit the flooding of floors or the flowing of water across working or walking areas or into difficult-to-clean areas, or otherwise create a nuisance. Correct overflowing of floor drain.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Onserved that the floor under the bar sink was soiled with debris, and the floor under the grille area was soiled.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: Observed that there was some flaking or peeling paint in the employee rest room, below the sink.  750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings. Scrape and repaint wall in this area.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Chili in walkin cooler made on 11/23 was at 50F in the middle. Cooked potentially hazardous foods must be properly cooled from 135F to 70F in 2 hours and from 70F to 41F/below in an additional 4 hours. Total cooling time must not exceed 6 hours. Chili was discarded in the trash during the inspection. **Separate large batches in to multiple containers and use ice baths and ice wands to cool foods quickly. Check temperatures periodically during cooling process to ensure proper cooling of foods.**

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text: 750.650 - All three cutting boards in prep area were pitted to the point they are not easily cleanable and have mold buildup. Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices. Clean and resurface the cutting boards or replace them with cutting boards that are in good repair/smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text: 750.690 - A) Upright silver freezer had a broken fan cover. Repair the fan cover. B) Wooden table at wait station had chipped paint. Repaint the table. C) Middle door of 3 door freezer in storage area was missing a handle. Replace the missing handle. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - Dirty wiping cloths, some of which were wet, were observed on counters throughout the kitchen. Wet wiping cloths must be properly stored in sanitizer solution between uses to inhibit the growth of microorganisms. Dirty wiping cloths must be stored in proper soiled laundry storage area. Properly store dirty and in use wiping cloths.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) soda guns and where nozzles attached (black mold); B) coffee spout (wait station); C) baffle of salad shooter; D) can opener; & D) magnetic knife strip. Wash, rinse, and sanitize the above items and all food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris and prevent cross contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) (R) plastic carts; B) (R) counter below order window; C) floor fan in kitchen; D) heat lamp; E) cook line - grill drip tray, fryers, and sides of equipment;  F) #10 can rack; G) produce cooler - back wall top & fan cover; H) dust pan; I) walkin cooler - shelves & fan covers; J) bottom inside pizza prep cooler; K) inside oven; & L) prep table beneath magnetic knife strip. Clean the above items and all non-food contact surfaces to eliminate buildup of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text: 750.850 - A) Soup spoon storage container was soiled. B) Gray utensil storage tub in kitchen had crumbs in it. C) Plates and bowls on top shelf in kitchen were not covered or inverted. Clean and sanitized equipment and utensils must be stored in a manner that protects them from potential contamination. Clean the plastic containers used for storing clean utensils and soup spoons daily/as needed and keep them covered between uses. Also, cover plates and bowls with plastic wrap or foil at night or provide some other form of overhead cover for dishes on top shelf.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text: 750.1060 - Faucet at 3 compartment sink had a leak. All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Have a licensed plumber repair the faucet in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text: 750.1110 - A) Banquet room restrooms were in general soiled. Floors were dirty and toilets had fecal particles in them. B) Women's restroom sinks were soiled. Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair. Clean the banquet restrooms after every event, and check them area daily. If employees use the banquet area restrooms they must clean up after themselves. Clean handsinks and faucets nightly and all other restroom fixtures.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) (R) Storage room (across from walkin) had a hole in floor (drain) that was dirty inside and not covered. Clean inside the hole and place a cover over the hole. B) (R) Floor drains were in general soiled at the bar. Clean all floor drains daily/as needed. C) Floors in general were soiled under coolers in the bar, dry storage in (under soda syrup boxes), dish area (drains, cover, and coving), in storage area by mopsink, and in the alcohol cooler. Clean floors, drains, drain covers and coving in the above areas and throughout daily/as needed.
